title: Trace Tables and Dry Runs
learningObjectives: Define a dry run and trace table.
Trace assignments, branches, and loop iterations.
Locate logic errors by identifying the first divergence.
Use normal and boundary inputs to verify an algorithm.

understand.concept: A dry run manually executes an algorithm using chosen input values. A trace table records variables, conditions, iteration counts, and outputs as they change. It helps check logic without running a compiler or debugger.
understand.whyItMatters: Tracing makes hidden state changes and branch choices visible, helping identify incorrect updates, off-by-one errors, and missing cases early.
understand.analogy: Following a board game's moves on paper to check whether the rules and sequence lead to the expected position.
understand.analogyLimit: Manual traces are useful but can be slow for large programs or many inputs; automate tests or use debugging tools for broader coverage.

explain.narrative: Choose a small input, list variables, and record each statement or iteration in order. Evaluate conditions, show updates, and note output. Compare the trace with the expected behavior and inspect the first step that differs. Repeat with a boundary or unusual input.

examples.title: Count loop iterations
examples.explanation: Tracing loop condition and update shows four iterations.

examples.title: Follow a branch
examples.code: const n=7; let label=''; if(n%2===0) label='even'; else label='odd'; console.log(label);
examples.explanation: The trace checks the condition and follows only the selected branch.

examples.title: Track an array index
examples.code: const a=[4,9,2]; let sum=0; for(let i=0;i<a.length;i++) sum+=a[i]; console.log(sum);
examples.explanation: A table can record index, element, and running sum for each iteration.

examples.title: Dry-run boundary input
examples.code: let remaining=3; remaining--; remaining--; remaining--; console.log(remaining);
examples.explanation: Tracing the final decrement confirms the value reaches the boundary.

commonMistakes: Missing a loop iteration or stopping check.

guidedTask.title: Guided practice: Trace a running total
guidedTask.instructions: Manually trace a loop that adds numbers from 1 through 4.
steps: Create columns for iteration, current number, and running total.
Record the condition when the loop ends.
Compare the final total to the expected value.
guidedTask.starterCode: // Use a paper or text trace table; no playground is required.

independentTask.title: Independent practice: Trace a small decision-and-loop algorithm
independentTask.instructions: Trace an algorithm that counts how many values in a list are positive.
requirements: Choose a short list containing positive, zero, and negative values.
Create columns for index, value, condition, and count.
Explain the final count and test an empty-list case.

hints: Write the initial state before the first step.
Update one variable at a time.
Check the first mismatch before changing the algorithm.
